GRU4Rec’s strongest established objectives are BPR-max and cross-entropy. BPR-max emphasizes high-scoring negatives: with w=softmax(negative scores), its loss is −log Σj wj·sigmoid(spositive−sj) + λΣj wj·sj². This differs from averaging weighted log-sigmoid losses; score regularization is a separate component. The official implementation also supports popularity-powered sampling and logQ correction for cross-entropy. These provide distinct experimental axes: objective, sampling distribution, and score penalty. [GRU4Rec paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official repository](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).

Recent evidence supports dataset-dependent sampling choices rather than universally harder negatives. A 2024 sequential-recommendation study found uniform sampling strongest on head items, while popularity-based sampling could improve balance across popularity bands at some aggregate accuracy cost. False negatives remain a concern: high model scores alone do not establish irrelevance. UFNRec studies this issue using teacher/student training; that mechanism should not be imported into this constrained single-model experiment. [2024 sampling study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116).

Suggested controlled comparison: retain the GRU backbone and match negative IDs/counts between BPR-max and sampled cross-entropy; then separately vary uniform versus popularity-mixture pools, BPR-max score regularization, and cross-entropy sampling correction using the actual proposal probabilities. Exclude padding, target collisions, and observed training positives. Treat absolute-event-recency weighting as a separate timestamp-based hypothesis, initially disabled. Weaker sampled margins in Movies_and_TV and Electronics motivate these tests but do not establish gains. Select solely by fixed four-category macro validation HR@10, retaining one trained checkpoint per category.
